rows.title: Policy groups urge CT to intensify saving to end pension debt
rows.standfirst: A Yankee Institute report says tens of billions in pension debt could be erased by 2038 if all the economic variables break CT’s way.

rows.title: United Way: Nearly 40% of CT households faced poverty in 2022
rows.standfirst: A CT family of four needed at least $108,324 to survive in 2022, the United Way said. Of all households, nearly 40% fell below the threshold.

rows.title: Scanlon to lawmakers: Tread carefully with CT budget controls
rows.standfirst: Scanlon, who had spoken only of maintaining the controversial system of budget controls prior to this week, acknowledged that a reform movement is growing.

rows.title: Candidates try to guide voters through labyrinthine CT budget debate
rows.standfirst: CT’s fiscal controls, while impossible to ignore, don’t translate well to the campaign trail. So how are politicians framing the discussion?

rows.title: Could CT budget face emergency cuts despite plan to save $1.2B?
rows.standfirst: CT expects to set aside $1.2 billion to pay down pension debt, but projects nearly $400 million in General Fund cost overruns.

rows.title: CT retirement benefit debate looms large over next term
rows.standfirst: Debates once centered on whether CT was too generous with retiree benefits. Now, there’s concern that they’ve been severely whittled down.
